clue.text: Minor inconveniences securing a rotating tool with bolts

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other pieces fast inside it, as a fastening secures something

parts.note: to bolt is to run away, so bolts here is the verb flees
taken as written
a drill bit is the tool that spins in a drill

explanation.surface: A workman's bolts gripping a spinning drill attachment, with nothing worse than small annoyances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolts' looks like hardware next to a tool, but it is the verb meaning runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea bites are small itchy nuisances, used figuratively for trivial irritations.

clue.text: More than one gathering about fifty plants

indicators.note: about means around, so the gatherings wrap around the fifty

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, a public gathering
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Several meetings held around fifty plants, perhaps at a garden club.
explanation.walkthrough: FORA, the Latin plural of forum, goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Accept total humiliation when leader in race has tied at swimming

indicators.note: the letters are swimming about, all at sea, so they are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A competitor concedes utterly when the front-runner of a swimming race finishes level.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first letter of race with the words tied and at; 'swimming' looks like the race's sport but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat dirt is an idiom for submitting to humiliation or grovelling.

clue.text: Top of bun too sweet for baked item

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
icky means sickly, cloyingly sweet

explanation.surface: The glaze on a bun is too sugary for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: BICKY is informal British for a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicky is a colloquial word for a biscuit, which is a baked snack.

clue.text: Recital of letter on page, one of many read by fortune-teller?

definitions.text: one of many read by fortune-teller?

indicators.note: a recital is something spoken, so the letter is given by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the letter T, said out loud
a leaf is a page of a book

explanation.surface: Reading out a letter on a page, a clairvoyant gives a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea-leaf reading, or tasseography, is fortune-telling from leaves left in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller reading a cup interprets the many leftover leaves, each one a leaf of tea.

clue.text: Instrument hit while holding end of baton up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hit is slang for a murder by a contract killer

indicators.note: the word for while holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I walked'

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: An orchestral percussion piece is struck while the conductor raises his baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like striking a drum, but it is a gangland killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its lower head.

clue.text: Shipwrecked rats!

indicators.note: the word carries its own signal: the ship it names is wrecked, so those letters are scrambled

parts.note: the first part of the word Shipwrecked supplies the letters to be wrecked

explanation.surface: Rats leaving a sinking ship, as in the proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word Shipwrecked splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Pish and rats are both exclamations of annoyance or contempt.

clue.text: 24 in lobby consumed by horrid matter

indicators.note: the outer word eats the other, enclosing it

parts.note: pus is the unpleasant matter in an infected wound
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: Something in a foyer swallowed up by disgusting material.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is MEMBER, here in its anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Member is a euphemism for the male organ, which a phallus is.

clue.text: Three females I led astray joining 10 24's club

parts.note: she plus F and F, three ways of indicating a female

indicators.note: the letters go astray, wandering into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Wednesday Addams is a member of the Addams Family, the theme

explanation.surface: Three women misled by a man joining a family member's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Several entries are members of the Addams Family. Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield Wednesday is a professional football club based in Sheffield, England.

clue.text: 10 24 I see, one loading weapon shortly

indicators.note: the weapon is loaded with the other letters, which go inside it
cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mortar is a short-barrelled gun
IC is the familiar abbreviation of 'I see'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A family member notices someone loading a gun in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Morticia Addams is the matriarch of the Addams Family.
explanation.definitionFit: Morticia is the mother in the Addams Family, so she is one of its relatives.

clue.text: Grand Inquisitor chasing old lady after revolution, aghast!

indicators.note: the inquisitor comes behind, chasing what goes before it
once revolved, the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for a mother, an old lady
Azed, the Observer setter, took his name from the Spanish Grand Inquisitor Don Diego de Deza

explanation.surface: A torturer pursues an elderly woman who has spun round, and she is horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the long-running Observer crossword's pseudonym, A. Deza reversed; Deza was a Grand Inquisitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed and aghast both describe someone struck with astonishment.

clue.text: Mummy gutted, if embalmer working for daddy, say?

indicators.note: letters at work are moved about into a new order
a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters survive the gutting
taken as written

explanation.surface: An embalmer disembowelling a mummy stands in for the father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' and 'daddy' look like a parent pair, but mummy is the embalmed body.
explanation.definitionFit: A daddy is one example of a relative, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Military command certainly abandoned after first of evacuations

indicators.note: the following pieces come after that letter
only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used
yes, certainly
left means abandoned, as in left behind

explanation.surface: An army order: certainly abandon the place after the first evacuations.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes left is a parade-ground order to turn the head to the left in salute.

clue.text: Little jerk behind card sharp

indicators.note: the jerk comes behind the card

parts.note: an ace is a playing card
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A twitching cheat lurking behind a card sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' reads as a cheat, but sharp is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means like vinegar, so sour or sharp in taste.

clue.text: Legion after desertion of a nobleman?

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
less as a suffix means without, deserted by

explanation.surface: An army left after a nobleman deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: A legion is a vast number, as in 'their number is legion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means innumerable, too many to count.

clue.text: Wind in European city, fleece put on

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is put on the first, following it

parts.note: Cork is a city in Ireland
to fleece or screw someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A gale in an Irish city, and a woolly jumper pulled on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' and 'wind' suggest clothing and weather; fleece means cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To corkscrew is to wind or twist in a spiral.

clue.text: Something precious penned by 10 24, English author

indicators.note: penned means enclosed in a pen, so the precious thing sits inside

parts.note: Uncle Fester is a member of the Addams Family
or is gold in heraldry, a precious metal

explanation.surface: A relative writes something precious about an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing, which suits the author, but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: C. S. Forester was the English novelist who created Horatio Hornblower.

clue.text: 10 24 defending the homestead with university reformers

indicators.note: the family member stands around the other letters, guarding them

parts.note: Lurch is the Addams Family's towering butler
taken as written
a ranch is a farm homestead

explanation.surface: A relative protecting the farm and the college from reformers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lutheran Church arose from Martin Luther's Protestant Reformation.

clue.text: Spaced out, secure gymnastic equipment

parts.note: high means intoxicated, spaced out
to bar a door is to secure it

explanation.surface: A stoned gymnast fastening the apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: The high bar is the horizontal bar apparatus in men's artistic gymnastics.

clue.text: Date on end of contract roughly marked

indicators.note: the letters are arranged roughly, not in their original order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A date written at the end of an agreement in rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated means written down in notation, so marked on the page.

clue.text: Discontented people in those riding scooters: these are similar

indicators.note: the people go in the scooter riders

parts.note: Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture known for riding motor scooters

indicators.note: with its content removed, only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: only its first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: Unhappy folk among the scooter gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' wants to mean unhappy, but it empties the word people.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopeds are light motorbikes much like scooters, so they are similar machines.

clue.text: Fortune invested in training, child finally played guitar

indicators.note: the fortune is put inside, as money is invested in a venture

parts.note: PE is physical education, school training
luck is fortune

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Money spent on lessons, the youngster at last strummed a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck strings is to play a guitar by picking them with the fingers.

clue.text: Leg position, requirement for play

parts.note: a stage is one leg of a journey
to set is to position

explanation.surface: A cricketing or dance leg position needed for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage set is the scenery needed for a theatre play.

clue.text: See 16
Reportedly cold country

indicators.note: as reported, it is heard rather than seen, so it sounds like the word

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: A frosty nation, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a South American nation.

clue.text: Sharp, like a container?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: can-like, as -y makes an adjective from can

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up adjective, can plus -y, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and quick-witted, especially in a Scottish or northern usage.

clue.text: See 10
10 24 wrapping up 10 judgment

indicators.note: the outer word wraps round the other

parts.note: Thing is the disembodied hand in the Addams Family
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A relative bundling the family up in a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking can mean opinion or reasoning, as in 'to my thinking'.

clue.text: Addict, monarch of republic?

parts.note: the US is a republic
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A drug-dependent king of a state with no king.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen; 'monarch of republic' is a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug taker.
